risks.title: Declining demand for printing
risks.score_rationale: HP explicitly mentions challenges related to declining demand for printing products due to digitization and hybrid work, as well as competition from non-OEM alternatives. This represents a significant risk to the Printing segment.

risks.title: AI adoption risks
risks.score_rationale: HP identifies in its strategic risk factors that the execution of its strategy depends on its ability to develop, manufacture, and market innovative solutions. As AI is central to its 2026 strategy, execution or adoption failures constitute material risks.

risks.title: Supply chain issues and cost volatility
risks.score_rationale: The 10-K report explicitly mentions supply chain challenges, including inflationary pressures on memory and storage costs, new tariffs imposed since April 2025 not fully offset by pricing actions, and single-source suppliers for certain Printing components.

risks.title: Increased competition and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: HP explicitly notes a competitive pricing environment, entry of new competitors with alternative technologies, and targeted competitive pressure from existing players in Personal Systems. Changes in the competitive landscape threaten market share.

risks.title: Macroeconomic risks and currency volatility
risks.score_rationale: HP identifies persistent geopolitical tensions, market uncertainty, exchange rate volatility, and inflationary pressures. With 65% of revenue generated outside the U.S., currency volatility represents a material risk to financial results.

risks.title: Transformation strategy execution challenges
risks.score_rationale: HP acknowledges that strategy execution depends on multiple factors including cost optimization, product innovation, IP protection, R&D investments, and business model evolution. The Fiscal 2026 plan introduces new three-year objectives.

ai_positioning.summary: HPQ has no significant mentions regarding artificial intelligence or machine learning in the provided excerpts from the 10-K/20-F document.
